name: International Policy (MA)

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.desc:
​​To earn the MA in International Policy, students must complete a minimum of 80 units. The degree requirements are as follows:
Core Curriculum (27 units)
All core courses are fundamental and must be completed during the first year, with the exception of INTLPOL 300S, which is required in the Winter Quarter of the second year.
Subplan (20 units)
Students must complete one subplan consisting of:

• Two required courses, completed during the first year

• At least three additional courses selected from the approved Subplan Elective Courses list
Customized Electives (24 units)
Students must complete 24 units of elective coursework selected to support and broaden their course of study. These courses must be broadly related to international policy and may include approved coursework across the University.
Capstone (9 units)
The fundamental capstone requirement consists of:

• The Policy Change Studio, a two-quarter sequence taken in Winter and Spring of the second year

• The associated Field Research course, taken in Spring Quarter of the second year
Students who matriculated prior to Autumn Quarter 2026 should refer to the Archived Bulletins for applicable degree requirements.

rules.name: Core Courses
rules.desc: All core courses must be completed during the first year of the program (except INTLPOL 300S, which is required during winter quarter of the second year). The only exception to the other core courses is for coterm, dual, or joint degree students who have conflicts with requirements in their other degree programs. In this instance, prior approval from MIP is required to move a core course to the second year. Note the additional guidance on first-year core courses:
rules.notes:
• INTLPOL 301A and INTLPOL 301B are a sequenced series in autumn and winter of the first year.

• Students are required to enroll in INTLPOL 300A, INTLPOL 301A, and INTLPOL 302 for autumn quarter.

• Students are required to enroll in INTLPOL 301B for winter quarter.

• Students are required to enroll in INTLPOL 306 and INTLPOL 307 for spring quarter.

• Students are required to enroll in INTLPOL 300S for winter quarter of the second year.

rules.name: Subplans
rules.desc:
The Ford Dorsey Master’s in International Policy (MIP) offers four subplans:

• Cyber Policy and Security (CYBER)

• Energy, Natural Resources, and the Environment (ENRE)

• Governance and Development (GOVDEV)

• International Security (ISEC)
Students must select one subplan and complete a minimum of five courses totaling at least 20 units. Each subplan includes two required courses that must be completed during the first year. In addition, students must complete at least three additional approved elective courses from the relevant Subplan Elective Course list.
Complete details for each subplan are provided in the individual subplan sections below.

rules.name: Customized Electives (24 units)
rules.desc:
Students must complete a minimum of 24 units of Customized Electives.
Customized Electives provide students the opportunity to engage with academic offerings across the University and tailor their course of study to their individual academic and professional interests. All courses applied toward this requirement must be broadly related to international policy.
Students may fulfill this requirement through a variety of pathways, including but not limited to: enrollment in additional subplan courses; completion of certificate programs (e.g., Computational Social Science Certificate); enrollment in language courses; completion of coursework in a second subplan (informally); or a combination of courses across disciplines that support the student’s academic objectives.
Courses numbered below 100 may not be applied toward graduate degree requirements, in accordance with University policy. In addition, activity courses, as well as performance and visual arts courses, do not satisfy MIP degree requirements.

Practical Training
Students may participate in an internship or other supervised practical experience that complements their degree program and subplan. With program approval, a maximum of 3 units of practical training may be applied toward the Customized Electives requirement.
During the academic year (Autumn, Winter, and Spring Quarters), students enroll in the designated Practical Training course (INTLPOL 298: Practical Training). A separate Practical Training course is offered during Summer Quarter (INTLPOL 298S: Practical Training). Both courses satisfy the academic enrollment requirement for Curricular Practical Training (CPT) for eligible students in F-1 status.
Students requesting enrollment in a Practical Training course for CPT purposes must submit the MIP CPT Proposal by the second Friday of the academic quarter in which they intend to enroll.
Additional information regarding eligibility, enrollment procedures, and CPT requirements is available on the MIP website and in the MIP Student Handbook.

rules.name: Capstone
rules.desc:
The Policy Change Studio serves as the capstone experience for the MIP program. In this fundamental course, student teams work under faculty supervision with external partners from industry, government, and the nonprofit sector to address complex policy challenges. The capstone is project-based and emphasizes the development of feasible, implementation-oriented solutions for real-world clients.
Course Enrollment Requirements
Students enroll in the Policy Change Studio over Winter Quarter and Spring Quarter of the second year, for a total of 8 units.
In addition, students enroll in the associated field research component course during Spring Quarter of the second year.
The MIP Capstone is a fundamental component of the degree program and exceptions are not permitted under any circumstances.
rules.notes:
• Students enroll in INTLPOL 310 for both winter quarter and spring quarter of the program’s second year, for a total of eight units.

• Additionally, students enroll in INTLPOL 310A, the field research component, for spring quarter of the program’s second year.

rules.name: Program Proposal in spring of year 1, and Graduation Program Proposal by week 2 of the graduation quarter
rules.desc:
Program Proposal
Students must submit a MIP Master's Degree Program Proposal during the Spring Quarter of their first year of study. As part of this requirement, students must schedule a 30-minute advising appointment with the MIP Academic Services Team to review their academic progress and develop a plan for completing the remaining degree requirements.
The University requires all graduate students to have an approved program proposal on file with their degree program. Students who do not complete this requirement will have an enrollment hold placed on their student account until the requirement has been satisfied.
Please see the Graduate Advising page for additional details.
Graduation Program Proposal
Students must submit a MIP Graduate Program Proposal in the quarter in which they intend to graduate, or no later than the second week of the intended graduation quarter. This proposal serves as formal confirmation of the student’s academic plan and degree completion status.
Failure to submit the required Graduation Program Proposal by the stated deadline will result in denial of the application to graduate.

rules.name: Subplan Overview
rules.desc:
Subplan Requirements
Students must select one subplan and complete a minimum of five courses within that subplan, totaling at least 20 units. Each subplan includes two required courses, which must be completed during the first year of study. In addition, students must complete at least three approved subplan elective courses, selected from the subplan elective course list.
The list of approved subplan elective courses is available below and on the MIP website.
Subplan Selection
Upon matriculation, students will see their assigned subplan reflected in Axess based on the selection submitted at the time of admission. Students will be asked to confirm or update their subplan prior to matriculation in Autumn Quarter; this designation is used to assign faculty advisors.
Students may request to change their subplan through the end of the first academic year, subject to approval by the MIP Assistant Director for Academic and Student Affairs.
Approved subplan changes must be processed through the Declaration or Change to a Field of Study for Graduate Students (Subplan Change) eForm in Axess.
Subplan Course Planning
Required subplan courses must be completed during the first year of study unless an exception is approved due to unavoidable scheduling conflicts. Approval to defer a required subplan course to the second year must be granted in advance by the MIP Assistant Director for Academic and Student Affairs.
No exemptions are permitted for required subplan courses. Coterminal students who have previously completed a required subplan course as part of their undergraduate program should consult with MIP regarding alternative course options to avoid duplication.
All required subplan courses must be taken for a letter grade. A limited number of subplan elective courses may be taken on a pass/fail basis, subject to University and MIP program grading policies. Courses numbered below 100 may not be applied toward graduate degree requirements.
Subplan Course Petition Process
Twice per year, MIP accepts petitions to add courses to the list of approved subplan electives. This process allows students to propose courses for review by MIP leadership and faculty subject-matter leads for the relevant subplan.
Petition submission timelines will be announced in advance of each review cycle. Students must submit complete course information, including a syllabus and a written rationale for inclusion.
Course review criteria include:

• Alignment with subplan learning objectives

• Student-provided rationale for inclusion

• Recency and consistency of course offerings

• Graduate-level designation (generally courses numbered 200 and above)

• Availability of a letter grade option (except in GSB, Law, and School of Medicine courses where applicable)

• Teaching evaluations, when available
Skills-based or primarily experiential courses are typically classified as Customized Electives rather than subplan electives.
Approved courses will be added to the official subplan elective list. Students may apply a course retroactively toward subplan requirements if it is approved after the course has been completed.
The elective course list includes both currently offered and historically approved courses, maintained as part of the program record in accordance with University policy. A current list of active courses is available on the MIP website.

rules.name: At least 15 units at the Vienna School of International Studies, with course selections approved by MIP
rules.desc:
Stanford MIP-Vienna School of International Studies Academic Exchange
The Stanford MIP–Vienna School of International Studies Academic Exchange is a one-quarter (Autumn Quarter) exchange program between the Ford Dorsey Master’s in International Policy (MIP) and the Diplomatische Akademie Wien – Vienna School of International Studies (DA). Each year, two second-year students from each institution are selected through a competitive application process to participate in the exchange. Selected students receive fellowships to study at the partner institution, where they enroll as full-time students, participate in academic and extracurricular activities, and engage in the intellectual community of the host institution.
Academic Policies
Students participating in the exchange must complete all requirements of the MIP MA curriculum. The minimum number of Stanford units required for graduation is reduced to 65 units for students participating in the exchange.
In addition to the Stanford unit requirement, students must complete the equivalent of at least 15 units (typically four or more full-time courses) at the Vienna School of International Studies. These courses will apply towards the subplan electives or Customized Electives. As such, the two required subplan courses must be completed at Stanford.
MIP exchange participants must submit their proposed DA course selections to the MIP Academic Services Team for approval no later than the end of the first week of classes in the Autumn Trimester at the DA.
Students are strongly encouraged to carefully evaluate how coursework completed at the DA will apply toward MIP degree requirements and to consider the implications of spending one quarter away from Stanford.
Enrollment and Transcript Policy
While participating in the exchange, students remain active in their Stanford academic program; however, they are not considered enrolled at Stanford during the exchange quarter. Students receive an official transcript from the Vienna School of International Studies for the Autumn Trimester. The exchange is not reflected on the Stanford transcript.
Additional Information
Further details are available on the Stanford–Vienna Academic Exchange page of the MIP website.

rules.name: Dual or joint degree unit allocation (54 MA units for MBA and JD students, up to 45 units shared with the MPP)
rules.desc:
Allocation of Credit for Dual Degree Programs involving the Master of Arts in International Policy
Dual Degree: GSB-MBA/INPOL-MA
The dual MBA/MA program is typically completed in approximately three academic years, depending on prior academic preparation and quantitative background.
Admissions decisions are made independently by each program. Units may not be double-counted toward both degrees; coursework must be applied to either the MBA or the MA degree requirements, but not both.
Students in the dual degree program must complete:

• 90 units for the MBA

• 54 units for the MA in International Policy, including the following requirements:

• Core curriculum: 27 units

• Subplan: 18 units

• Capstone: 9 units
Students should consult both the MBA Program Office and the MIP Assistant Director for Academic and Student Affairs for additional guidance.
Dual Degree: ENVRES-MS/INPOL-MA
Students must complete all degree requirements for both programs, including 80 units for the MA in International Policy and 45 units for the MS in Environment and Resources. Completing the MS degree typically requires at least three additional quarters of study beyond the time required to complete the MA.
Joint Degree: LAW-JD/INPOL-MA
The joint JD requires 111 units, and the MA in International Policy requires 54 units. Students enrolled in the joint program must complete the following MIP requirements:

• Core curriculum: 27 units

• Subplan 18 units

• Capstone 9 units
Students who begin their studies at Stanford Law School may, with MIP approval, complete the required statistics sequence through the Law School in place of the INTLPOL statistics sequence. However, this option is not recommended, as the Law School sequence typically includes a single statistics course, whereas the INTLPOL sequence consists of two courses that provide broader methodological preparation (including training in R) for the MIP capstone.
Students who elect this option may be at a disadvantage in capstone preparation. Prior approval from MIP is required. Any resulting unit adjustments will be applied to subplan requirements as appropriate.
In addition, Customized Electives are not required for joint JD students who matriculate first in the Law School. In some cases, Customized Electives may also be waived for students who matriculate first in MIP, subject to program approval.
Joint Degree: MPP/INPOL-MA
The MPP requires 90 units, and the MA in International Policy requires 80 units. In approved joint degree programs, up to 45 units (or one year of residency) may be applied toward both degrees. As a result, the total unit requirement for the joint degree may be reduced by up to 45 units compared to the combined requirements of the two individual degrees.
The MPP/MA joint degree program requires a three-year residency, reflecting this overlap in coursework and program requirements.
The Public Policy Program encourages the development of a strong intellectual, professional, and social cohort experience. For this reason, joint degree students are strongly encouraged to complete one academic year of full-time study dedicated exclusively to the Public Policy Program, rather than distributing Public Policy coursework across multiple years of study.

rules.name: Coterminal MA: 70 units, with 14 units of Customized Electives
rules.desc:
Coterminal Master's Degree Requirements
Coterminal students admitted to MIP must complete the following requirements to earn the MA in International Policy:

• Core curriculum: 27 units

• Subplan: 20 units, including:

• Two required courses

• At least three additional courses selected from the approved subplan elective list

• Customized Electives: 14 units

• Capstone: 9 units
The minimum total number of units required to complete the coterminal MA in International Policy is 70 units.

gpa:
To remain in good academic standing and to be eligible for the conferral of the MA degree, MIP students must maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0. Students who fail to maintain good academic standing, whether by falling below the minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 or by failing to make satisfactory progress toward the degree, will be placed on academic probation. Continued failure to meet academic standards may result in dismissal from the University. Students experiencing academic difficulties are strongly encouraged to consult with the MIP Assistant Director for Academic and Student Affairs as early as possible to discuss available support and strategies for returning to good academic standing.
Please review the details on Minimum Progress Requirements for Graduate Students.
grading:
Students must take the following courses for a letter grade:

• MIP Core Courses

• Exceptions: INTLPOL 300A and 300S, both of which are only offered as Satisfactory/No Credit

• MIP Capstone Courses

• Exception: INTLPOL 310A, which is only offered as Satisfactory/No Credit

• MIP Subplan (i.e., Area of Specialization) Required Courses
Students may apply up to 10 pass/fail units toward the Subplan Electives and Customized Electives. (Note: This is a combined total).

• The 10-unit limit includes pass/fail courses taken at the: Graduate School of Business; School of Earth, Energy, and Environmental Science; School of Education; School of Engineering; School of Medicine; School of Sustainability; and School of Humanities and Sciences. This also includes Law School courses taken as: Mandatory Pass/Restricted Credit/Fail.
Students assigned a grade of Incomplete ("I") are subject to the MIP program's deadlines for completing outstanding coursework. These deadlines are more restrictive than the University's standard policy. The required completion schedule is as follows:

• Autumn and winter quarters: Incomplete grades must be completed no later than June 30 of the same academic year.

• Spring quarter: Incomplete grades must be completed no later than August 30 of the same academic year.

• Summer quarter: Incomplete grades must be completed no later than December 30 of the same calendar year.
Students are also responsible for coordinating the course completion with the instructor(s) and apprising the MIP Assistant Director for Academic and Student Affairs of progress.
Students who accrue three or more grades of Incomplete ("I") or who carry Incomplete grades over multiple academic quarters will be placed on academic probation. An exception may be granted when the student's circumstances are attributable to documented personal or medical reasons. Documentation must be provided by Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS), the Office of Accessible Education (OAE), or Vaden Health Center.
policies:
Courses numbered below 100 may not be applied toward graduate degree requirements. A maximum of 12 undergraduate-level units (generally numbered 100-199, with the exception of History and Political Science courses numbered 100-299) may be taken toward the INPOL-MA
Activity courses (e.g., tennis and weightlifting), performance and visual arts courses (e.g., piano, studio arts, and dance), WELLNESS courses, and other courses numbered below 100 do not satisfy MIP degree requirements. Restrictions on English proficiency courses are described in English Proficiency Courses below.
Language Courses
Units earned in language courses may be applied only toward the Customized Electives requirement. Language courses numbered below 100 do not count toward MIP degree requirements, per University policy. Students seeking advanced language study should consult the Stanford Language Center regarding available graduate-level options, including enrollment in courses numbered 395, where appropriate.
English proficiency courses for international students do not count toward MIP degree requirements.
Students planning to apply language course units toward the MA degree must obtain approval from the MIP Assistant Director for Academic and Student Affairs before the Final Study List deadline for the applicable quarter.
Directed Readings
A directed reading is an independent study conducted under the guidance and supervision of a Stanford instructor. Additional information is available in Stanford Navigator, the Stanford Bulletin, and the MIP website.
Students may propose a directed reading to satisfy subplan or Customized Electives requirements when existing course offerings do not adequately support their academic or research objectives.
Directed Reading Limits
The following restrictions apply to directed reading courses:

• A maximum of 15 units of directed reading may be applied toward the MA degree.

• Of these, no more than 10 units may be applied toward subplan requirements.

• Any remaining directed reading units may be applied toward the Customized Electives requirement, subject to the 15-unit maximum.

• Students may enroll in a maximum of 5 units per directed reading course.

• All directed reading courses must be taken for a letter grade.
Proposal and Approval Process
Students must submit a MIP Directed Reading Proposal to the MIP Assistant Director for Academic and Student Affairs for approval. The proposal must include:

• The proposed topic of study

• A research or study plan

• Course requirements, including assignments and other deliverables

• Confirmation from the instructor (provided via signature or email confirmation)
Proposals must be submitted no later than the second Friday of the academic quarter in which the student intends to enroll. MIP will review each proposal and notify the student of its decision no later than two days before the Final Study List deadline.
If a proposal is approved, MIP will create a section of INTLPOL 299: Directed Reading for the supervising instructor. Students will enroll in the section corresponding to their instructor (e.g., INTLPOL 299-02: Directed Reading (Stoner, Kathryn)).
transferPolicy: Per university policy, students enrolled in this MA program may not apply external credits toward their degree requirements. The university’s general requirements, applicable to all graduate degrees at Stanford, are listed in Graduate Degrees.
reviewNotes: You choose one of four subplans. The audit checks the 80 graduate units, the seven core courses and the INTLPOL 310 capstone (twice, plus INTLPOL 310A) for a letter grade, the subplan's required courses (letter graded) and electives with at least 20 units, and 24 units of Customized Electives numbered 100 or above (at most 3 units of practical training). Courses below 100 and WELLNESS courses never count; at most 12 units at the 100-199 level, 15 units of directed reading (INTLPOL 299, letter graded) and 10 pass/fail elective units count. Checked by hand: the program proposal in spring of your first year and the graduation program proposal, the 3.0 GPA, that electives relate to international policy, directed reading proposals (at most 10 units in the subplan, 5 per course), language courses (Customized Electives only, with approval), and HISTORY or POLISCI 200-level courses against the 12 undergraduate units. Coterminal students who add the Coterminal MA section need 70 units instead of 80, and mark the Customized Electives met at 14 units. MBA and JD dual-degree students need 54 MA units; the audit still asks for 80, so check that allocation by hand. Vienna exchange students add their 15 Vienna units by hand.
